stories.headline: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva wins fourth term as President of Brazil
stories.body:
Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won a fourth term as President of Brazil [c1]. He defeated Flávio Bolsonaro in the election runoff [c1]. Lula won the runoff vote with 51.79% of the total vote [c2]. He defeated Flávio Bolsonaro by 4.4 million votes [c2].

Flávio Bolsonaro had won the first round of voting on October 4 [c3]. He received 47% of the vote in that round [c3]. Lula received 45% in the first round [c3].

Brazil's Supreme Court ordered voting hours extended nationwide by two hours on Sunday [c8]. Both presidential campaigns requested this extension [c8]. Lula's campaign asked for extended hours because of bus transportation issues in nine states [c9]. Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign cited heavy rain in southern Brazil [c9]. Supreme Electoral Court President Kássio Nunes Marques confirmed Lula's victory [c10]. He said the voting time extension did not change the outcome of the race [c10].

US President Donald Trump claimed without providing evidence that Brazil's election looked rigged [c11]. Trump also criticized the decision to extend voting hours [c11]. Flávio Bolsonaro's political party issued a statement [c12]. The party recognized the presidential result announced by the electoral court [c12]. But the party called for political debate on questions raised during the election [c12].

Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes banned Flávio Bolsonaro from leaving Brazil [c4]. Flávio Bolsonaro is a 45-year-old senator [c4]. Justice Moraes ordered him to give up his passports within 24 hours [c4]. This Supreme Court ruling relates to a criminal investigation [c5]. The investigation involves alleged money laundering with lawyer Willer Tomaz and betting companies [c5].

Flávio Bolsonaro said federal police gave him the travel ban order in Brasília [c6]. Police served the order outside the home of his father, Jair Bolsonaro [c6]. Former President Jair Bolsonaro is currently under house arrest [c6]. He is serving a 27-year prison sentence [c7]. He was convicted for plotting a coup after his 2022 election loss [c7].

The election result was unexpected [c13]. After the result, the São Paulo stock exchange opened 15% lower [c13]. The stock exchange later partially recovered [c13].

vocab.meaning: a second election held to decide a winner between top candidates
a person's house or official home
a formal decision in court that someone is guilty of a crime

stories.headline: Student List movement wins majority in Serbia parliamentary election
stories.body:
The opposition Student List movement won Serbia's parliamentary election with 52.45% of the vote [c14]. The Student List won 138 seats in the National Assembly [c14]. The Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia list received 39.2% of the vote [c15]. That list secured 103 seats [c15].

Outgoing President Aleksandar Vučić conceded defeat late on Sunday [c16]. His concession ended 14 years of rule by his Serbian Progressive Party [c16]. Vučić alleged the election result verified a revolution supported by European countries and the US deep state [c22].

The Student List movement formed after a railway station canopy collapsed in Novi Sad on November 1, 2024 [c17]. That collapse killed 16 people [c17].

Voter turnout reached 69% as over 4.4 million citizens voted [c18]. Turnout was 55.5% in December 2023 [c18].

The Student List trained at least 16,000 official controllers and mobile teams [c19]. They monitored for fraud like carousel voting and parallel lists [c19].

The movement is leaderless and has no hierarchy [c20]. Its candidates include academics, doctors, actors, and farmers without prior political experience [c20]. Prominent figures include cardiologist Ilija Srdanović, former central bank governor Dejan Šoškić, and chemistry professor Radomir Saičić [c21].

European Commissioner for Enlargement Marta Kos said a new chapter can begin for Serbia [c23]. She said the European Union door is open [c23]. Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said Russia hopes Serbia's new leadership sees cooperation with Russia as beneficial [c24].

vocab.meaning: admitted defeat in an election or contest
the percentage or number of people who vote in an election

stories.headline: Israel prepares for national election as West Bank displacements and regional tensions rise
stories.body:
Israel will hold a parliamentary election on October 27 to choose 120 members of the Knesset [c25]. A party or coalition needs 61 seats to establish a governing coalition [c25]. Polls show Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's far-right coalition trailing an opposition bloc [c26]. Retired general Gadi Eisenkot leads that opposition bloc [c26]. Neither side is projected to reach 61 seats [c26].

Netanyahu posted an AI-generated image of a nuclear cloud destroying Tel Aviv [c27]. He warned voters to elect him or face nuclear destruction from Iran [c27]. Israeli media reported a clash between Netanyahu and IDF Chief of Staff Lt Gen Eyal Zamir [c28]. Zamir requested a written military directive concerning Iran [c28]. Eisenkot said he would not allow the military to become a pawn for Netanyahu's political survival [c29].

Reports indicated Netanyahu tried to persuade US President Donald Trump to attack Iran [c30]. But Trump ruled out action until after the US midterm elections [c30].

Israeli forces detained an international delegation of 23 people at the border for nine hours [c31]. The group included UK MP Clive Lewis and Scottish MP Lara Bird [c31]. Israeli forces barred them from entering the West Bank [c31].

UN rights chief Volker Türk warned of ethnic cleansing after Israeli forces displaced over 3,000 Palestinians in Hebron [c32]. The displacement followed a checkpoint attack where two Palestinian gunmen killed two Israeli soldiers [c33]. The UN aid office recorded at least 160 Israeli settler attacks linked to the olive harvest in early October [c34].

vocab.meaning: a temporary alliance of political parties forming a government
a group of people chosen to represent an organization or country

stories.headline: Jordan launches airstrikes in Syria and arrests suspects after church attack
stories.body:
Jordanian security forces arrested three men following a shootout in the city of Karak [c37]. The shootout occurred at an abandoned house at dawn [c37]. Security forces arrested brothers Hazzah Zaidan Mohammad and Mishal Zaidan Mohammad, alongside Ahmad Sami Hussein [c37]. All three suspects were wounded in the shootout [c38]. Authorities seized a large cache of munitions [c38].

The arrests followed an attack during a funeral at St George's Church in Hammoud village [c35, c36]. Nine people died and over two dozen were wounded in that Friday attack [c35]. Public Security chief Maj Gen Obaidallah Abd Rabbo Al-Maayta described the attackers as extremist fighters acting independently [c39]. Jordanian Interior Minister Mazen al-Faraya said all suspects were Jordanians with no foreign collaboration [c43].

King Abdullah II declared three days of national mourning [c44]. He vowed to respond with an iron fist against terrorist ideologies [c44].

The Jordanian air force launched retaliatory airstrikes against armed groups in southern Syria [c40]. The health director in Syria's Daraa province reported that at least five civilians died in those strikes [c41]. But Syria's SANA news agency quoted the same official saying at least eight civilians were killed [c42].

Eight church attack victims were buried beside the church on Sunday [c45]. The ninth victim was buried in south Amman on Monday [c45].

vocab.meaning: done in order to pay back or get revenge for an attack

stories.headline: Election Commission defends voter roll revision process in Supreme Court
stories.body:
The Election Commission of India filed an affidavit in the Supreme Court to defend voter roll revisions [c46]. Deputy Election Commissioner Bhanu Prakash Yeturu filed the affidavit [c47]. He declared that the Chief Election Commissioner and two Election Commissioners unanimously decided on June 24, 2025, to conduct a nationwide voter roll revision [c46, c47].

Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi and others filed petitions challenging the process [c48]. Their challenge followed a news report alleging differences among the commissioners [c48]. The Indian Express reported that Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi objected to decisions 14 times [c56].

The Election Commission stated that letters sent by Sandhu and Joshi pertained to internal work allocation [c49]. An internal order issued on July 28 was never implemented [c50].

The commission denied amending Form 6 in its revision orders [c51]. It noted that only the Central Government can amend Form 6 [c52]. The new process requires voters to link their details with parents or grandparents in earlier rolls [c54].

Karnataka's final electoral roll will be published on October 27 [c57]. The state's voter count dropped from 5.54 crore to 4.54 crore after 1.07 crore names were deleted [c58]. Opposition parties protested to demand the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar [c61].

vocab.meaning: a written statement confirmed by oath for use as evidence in court
a formal written request made to an official body or court

stories.headline: Andhra Pradesh and Odisha prepare emergency response as Cyclone Arnab approaches
stories.body:
The Andhra Pradesh government released ₹27 crore to 20 districts to prepare for Cyclone Arnab [c63]. The money will support relief operations ahead of the cyclone's expected landfall on October 28 [c63].

The India Meteorological Department forecast that Cyclone Arnab will cross the coast between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam [c64]. The cyclone will also affect the Yanam coast [c64]. Winds are expected to reach sustained speeds of 115 to 125 kilometers per hour [c64]. Wind gusts could reach up to 140 kilometers per hour [c64].

At 5:30 am on October 26, Cyclone Arnab was 590 kilometers northwest of Sri Vijaya Puram [c74]. It was 610 kilometers southeast of Gopalpur [c74]. The storm was also 650 kilometers east-southeast of Visakhapatnam [c74].

Officials in Andhra Pradesh scheduled 4,711 pregnant women to move to safer healthcare facilities [c65]. A total of 30,043 fishing boats returned to harbours across the state [c66].

The Andhra Pradesh Department of Health prepared 6,431 emergency beds for the storm [c75]. The department readied 630 medical teams and 716 vehicles [c75]. Health authorities also stocked 13,101 doses of anti-snake venom across facilities [c76].

The Real Time Governance Society urged residents to report emergencies through WhatsApp [c77]. Residents can use the Mana Mitra platform for cyclone help [c77].

State Disaster Management Authority Director Prakhar Jain reported that 7 NDRF teams and 8 SDRF teams deployed to vulnerable districts [c71]. Fifteen NDRF teams deployed across vulnerable locations in Andhra Pradesh and Puducherry's Yanam district [c70].

In New Delhi, Cabinet Secretary T V Somanathan chaired a National Crisis Management Committee meeting [c67]. The committee reviewed cyclone preparedness across several states [c67].

The Andaman and Nicobar Islands ordered all schools to close until Tuesday [c68]. The Odisha government ordered schools, colleges, and Anganwadi centres to close on October 28 and 29 in six southern districts [c69].

Odisha Special Relief Commissioner Rajesh Prabhakar Patil said 135 cyclone shelters were prepared [c72]. The state also prepared 1,600 temporary accommodation centres [c72]. Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Majhi assigned eight state ministers to monitor preparations in different locations [c73].

vocab.meaning: the arrival of a tropical storm or cyclone over land
at risk of being easily hurt or damaged
